title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Terintambwe Mw'isi Itotahaye programme will work in Gasagara District, Rwanda. It aims to contribute to Concern Burundi and Concern Rwanda's Green Graduation thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to ensure households can sustainably meet their basic needs and have improved coping strategies through strengthened livelihoods which place value on the natural environment. The programme will support over 147,220 people living in extreme poor households, including landless, female-headed households, households with disabled members, Batwa community (ethnic minority) . This will be done through support to gain the necessary technical and business skills and financial literacy to be able to set up a suitable livelihood, improved human capital through coaching, mentoring and various lifeskills training, participation in gender transformative dialogue sessions and environmental enhancement and low carbon development measures are undertaken.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Vulnerable Households Experience Increased Levels of Food and Nutrition Security by Engaging in Income Generation along Food Value Chains. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: RM Mitigation 2: Energy conservation and demand-side efficiency are addressed through the promotion of clean cook stoves.RM Adaptation 2: With this allocation, the green graduation (GG) programme in Burundi will conduct a Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Assessment (CVCA) with the support of Head Office technical advisors. The purpose of the CVCA will be to support LTD GG communities to identify contextual climate shocks, stresses and changes that are impacting their ability to secure their basic needs. Communities will then be supported to develop Community Adaptation Action Plans (CAAPs) to address areas where communities can be empowered to make a positive difference in their resilience at the household or community level. The intention is that elements of these plans will be financed through the Climate Allocation in 2025.DRR 1: Green Graduation programmes are intended to build the resilience of communities and natural systems to a changing climate through awareness raising, capacity building, environmental awareness and promoting climate-smart activities.Aid to Environment 1: Concern’s Green Graduation programme added a 5th pillar to the traditional graduation model - the ‘green’ aspect which aims to improve environmental protection and stability through awareness raising, capacity building, assessing environmental impacts, reducing and managing environmental risks and increasing natural assets.Capacity Building 1: building the capacity of communities on climate-smart activities is necessary for environmental protection and sustainability.Gender Equality 1: a gender lens is applied at every stage and a gender transformative approach is taken to tackle harmful gender norms, attitudes and practices.Nutrition 1: Through improved agricultural practices (increasing yields) and messaging on nutrition, the nutritional status of HHs is improved.
